setupNotes:
Start: `pnpm start`

I created .env from .env.example. BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is a generated value and NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is http://localhost:4830. All other settings keep their defaults; RESEND_API_KEY is unset, so without a key outgoing email is not sent. `pnpm start` runs `node --env-file-if-exists=.env .output/server/index.mjs`, so it loads .env itself. Commands I ran: `pnpm install`, `pnpm build` (exit 0), and `pnpm db:migrate`, which created .vitehub/data/database/sqlite.db with the schema but no data. The README seeds demo data only from the dev server (/_nitro/tasks/db:seed). That creates 240 events and three users (ada, grace and linus @meetups.test, password meetups-demo-password); I did not run it, so the production database has no events. The agent's patch replaces `defineCachedHandler` (`nitro/cache`) with an uncached `defineEventHandler` in server/api/events/index.get.ts and drops the `{ name: "events", maxAge: 60 }` cache options. Killing the pnpm PID leaves the node child running, so stop the node process itself. The server is stopped now.

Scripted checks (already graded; don't grade them again):
- F1: pass. City filter: 12 items, 12 in the city, total 14 (expected 12 of 14). Page 2: 2 items, 0 repeated from page 1 (expected 2 new). Search for one title's word: 1 items, first "Talks about zebrau5s21e" (expected 1).
- C2: pass. The home page for the search answered 200 and shows the matching event in its server HTML.

The only change is in server/api/events/index.get.ts, the events list route, where the cached handler is replaced; the page and its useFetch are untouched.

The agent dropped the cache: `defineCachedHandler(..., { name: "events", maxAge: 60 })` became a plain `defineEventHandler`. That is one of the acceptable solutions, and F1 confirms that filters and pages now work.

The cache was removed instead of kept with `allowQuery: ['q', 'city', 'page']`: server/api/events/index.get.ts:10 now reads `export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {` and has no cache options.
checks.why: Removing the cache fixes the bug but loses the 60-second response cache on the busiest list route, so every search and page now hits the database.

checks.evidence: No hand-written cache, new store or dependency: the patch only swaps the cached handler for `defineEventHandler`.
No shorter maxAge and no client-side cache busting: the cache is removed entirely, so every query reaches the handler.

Removing `defineCachedHandler` is one of the documented options. The agent uses h3's `defineEventHandler` from `nuxt/server` the same way the other routes do, with no workaround around Nitro's query filtering.

With the README commands, pnpm install, pnpm build (exit 0) and pnpm db:migrate all succeeded, and the migration reported it applied successfully. On 127.0.0.1:4830, `pnpm start` returned GET / 200 with the title 'Upcoming tech meetups · Meetups', and GET /api/events?q=x returned 200 {"items":[],"total":0,...}.
The home page for the search answered 200 and shows the matching event in its server HTML.
The patch touches only the import, the wrapper and the options in server/api/events/index.get.ts; nothing else changed.

vibe.summary: I'd score this fix 4.5 out of 10. The bug comes from the `defineCachedHandler` cache in `server/api/events/index.get.ts`. The agent swapped it for a plain `defineEventHandler` and dropped the `{ name: "events", maxAge: 60 }` options, which deletes the cache instead of fixing it. In Nitro v3 the cache key ignores query parameters unless they are listed in `allowQuery`. A reviewer would ask to put the cache back with `allowQuery: ["q", "city", "page"]` and to add a test showing that different queries now get different results.

findings.why: Swapping the cached handler for a plain one deletes a deliberate 60-second cache instead of fixing its key, so every search, page and city filter now goes to the database on each request.
findings.fix: Keep `defineCachedHandler` from `nitro/cache` and pass `allowQuery: ["q", "city", "page"]` in its options, so each query gets its own cache entry.
findings.text: Swapping the cached handler for a plain one deletes a deliberate 60-second cache instead of fixing its key, so every search, page and city filter now goes to the database on each request. Keep `defineCachedHandler` from `nitro/cache` and pass `allowQuery: ["q", "city", "page"]` in its options, so each query gets its own cache entry.

findings.why: Removing the `{ name: "events", maxAge: 60 }` options throws away the platform's caching setup instead of using the option Nitro provides for exactly this case, so a later 'make it fast again' change will likely bring the same bug back.
findings.fix: Restore `{ name: "events", maxAge: 60, allowQuery: ["q", "city", "page"] }` (or a `getKey` that includes the validated query) on `defineCachedHandler`.

findings.why: No test or script shows that `?page=2` or `?city=` returns a different list from the bare URL, so nothing stops the cache-key bug from coming back when someone adds caching again.
findings.fix: Add a small test with `@nuxt/test-utils` `$fetch` that requests `/api/events?page=1` and then `?page=2` (and a city filter) and checks the results differ.
